author: Argus
title: A proxy keeps its whole upgrade authority in the runtime and nothing on-chain delays it
summary: The admin surface lives in the proxy bytecode itself, so whoever holds it replaces the logic in one transaction. No delay, timelock or queued-implementation selector is present, so nothing on-chain gives holders time to exit before a swap.

matcher.notes: upgradeTo(address) 0x3659cfe6, upgradeToAndCall(address,bytes) 0x4f1ef286, admin() 0xf851a440, implementation() 0x5c60da1b; absence checked over getMinDelay() 0xd33219b4 and delay() 0x6a42b8f8 only, so a bespoke timelock under another name is not detected. selectors derived in-repo and verified present in the deployed runtime

money_bound.expression: every balance the proxy holds, reachable by swapping the implementation

reproduction.expected: the proxy runtime carries admin(), implementation(), upgradeTo and upgradeToAndCall and no delay getter

confirmed_on.target: USDC proxy 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 chainId 1 (6 selectors in 2,186 bytes)
confirmed_on.equivalence: selector set derived in-repo from the live runtime, not from source

fix: State the upgrade path and who holds it; a delay contract is the usual mitigation.

evidence: the proxy is 2,186 bytes and carries 6 selectors, of which 5 are its admin surface
no getMinDelay() or delay() selector is present in the runtime
